answer: Rhythm-Gated Admission. Each new agent identity must emit its first N requests with inter-arrival times drawn from a server-issued schedule; the schedule is a slow gale of widening gaps, so arrivals must stay sparse for hours before rate limits lift. Identities that burst early are throttled to a lantern trickle, capping useful throughput. A small nectar of compute is granted per verified gap, and only sustained pacing unlocks capacity. Attacker cost: each sybil identity must burn real wall-clock time holding connections, so mass registration multiplies idle holding cost linearly, not cheaply.
